title: Event provenance, replayable transforms, and version tagging for analytics pipeline
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As we evolve telemetry event shapes across SDK/CLI/API clients, we lack a robust way to (1) record event provenance (which client + version + transform produced the event), (2) store deterministic, replayable transformation steps for historical data, and (3) tag events with explicit schema version metadata so downstream analytics and alerts are reproducible. Without this, rollbacks and regressions are hard to diagnose and analytics can silently diverge between historical and current pipelines.

This ticket establishes a pragmatic implementation: a lightweight event metadata envelope schema and a transform registry that records canonical transforms (canonicalization, enrichment, sampling rules) as immutable, versioned artifacts. The pipeline will attach provenance headers (client-id, client-version, transform-id, transform-version, producer-hash) and persist a compact transform descriptor so older events can be deterministically replayed through new or historical transforms as part of canarying and backfill. The work spans SDK/CLI tagging, gateway enrichment, ingestion pipeline plumbing, and a validation harness for replay correctness and quality comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: All incoming telemetry events include an envelope with: schema_version, client_id, client_version, transform_id, transform_version, and ingest_node_id where available.
A transform registry service (HTTP-read, append-only storage) is available and contains the initial canonicalization transforms for SDK v1.0, SDK v1.1, and CLI v0.9.
Ingestion path persists event provenance metadata alongside raw payload in parquet/avro (or equivalent) so replays can reconstruct original bytes and applied transforms.
A replay harness runs on historical data to reapply a different transform version and produces a quantitative diff report (field-level drift, tokenization differences, metric deltas).
SDKs and CLI emit schema_version and client_version in telemetry headers; documented in SDK changelog and release notes.
Automated canary replays run in sandbox pipeline for each transform registry update and must report a compatibility_score >= 95% before rollout to production.
Dashboards exist for provenance coverage (percent of events with full envelope), replay success rate, and transform compatibility scores.
Runbooks updated: how to perform a full reindex/replay for a time window, and how to rollback a transform version in the registry.
implementation_plan: 1) Add envelope fields to SDK/CLI telemetry: schema_version, client_id, client_version. Coordinate with SDK team for release flags. 2) Implement a small Transform Registry service (read-optimized, append-only) that stores transform descriptors (name, steps, canonical example, sha256). 3) Update ingestion pipeline to persist both raw event and applied_transform_id/version; store compact descriptor alongside partitions. 4) Build replay harness as a Spark/Beam job that can: (a) fetch raw event + original transform descriptor, (b) reapply specified transform version(s), (c) compute diffs and produce a compatibility score. 5) Add CI checks: linting for transforms, deterministic hashing, and unit tests for transform reversibility where applicable. 6) Canary rollout: run replay harness on last 7 days in sandbox, review compatibility dashboard, then toggle transform as default via registry. 7) Gradual rollout with metrics gating and rollback path documented.
testing_and_validation:
- Unit tests for transform functions (tokenization, normalization, enum mappings) with fixed seeds.
- Determinism tests: run same raw event through transform twice -> exact same bytes/hash.
- Replay integration test using sampled historical window for SDK v1.0 -> compute field-level deltas and assert no more than N% of events changed for critical fields.
- Canary replay job that runs nightly, writes compatibility_score metric to telemetry-dashboard.
- End-to-end smoke: client emits envelope, ingestion persists provenance, replay harness can rehydrate and reapply alternate transform. Links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-transform-registry/pull/137
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (sandbox): deploy transform registry to staging; update ingestion to persist transform metadata only in staging (no default change); run replay harness on 14 days. Phase 2 (canary): enable envelope emission in 5% of production traffic (SDK flag) and run sandbox replays to measure coverage. Phase 3 (gradual): after compatibility_score >=95 and SRE signoff, flip new canonical transform as default in registry and enable replay monitoring. Phase 4 (post-rollback): if compatibility_score drops or customer-impact metrics spike, use registry to pin older transform and trigger backfill audit. Timeline target to complete rollout by 2025-03-07.
rollback_plan:
- Registry supports pinning previous transform version as default.
- Ingestion reads default transform version from registry but stores applied_transform_id/version per event, so immediate rollback only affects new events.
- For historical correction, trigger backfill job that replays failed windows using pinned transform.
- Emergency: disable SDK envelope emission via feature flag and route to previous ingestion path if parsing errors detected.
monitoring_and_sla: Key metrics: provenance_coverage_pct, replay_success_rate, compatibility_score, transform_deploy_latency, field_delta_ratio. Alert if provenance_coverage_pct < 90% or compatibility_score < 90% for two consecutive canary runs. SLO: 99.9% successful ingestion when provenance envelope present. Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/telemetry/provenance
